issue_context.title: continue_on_error does not work for shell_command if there was a timeout
issue_context.body:
### The problem

`continue_on_error` does not work for `shell_command` if there was a timeout. As a result, automation stops and other services do not work.

configuration.yaml
```
shell_command:
  stop2_filezilla: ssh user@192.168.1.2 sc stop filezilla-server

```
automations.yaml
```
  - service: shell_command.stop2_filezilla
    continue_on_error: true

```
home-assistant.log

`Timed out running command: `ssh user@192.168.1.2 sc stop filezilla-server`, after: 60s
`
```

Source: helpers/script.py:507

First occurred: 12:03:01 PM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 12:03:01 PM

Traceback (most recent call last):

    stdout_data, stderr_data = await process.communicate()
                               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/asyncio/subprocess.py", line 201, in communicate
    stdin, stdout, stderr = await tasks.gather(stdin, stdout, stderr)
                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/asyncio/subprocess.py", line 181, in _read_stream
    output = await stream.read()
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

    await self._wait_for_data('read')
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/asyncio/streams.py", line 545, in _wait_for_data
    await self._waiter
asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
```

<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

as mentioned in [here](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/scripts/#continuing-on-error) the docs:

> Please note that continue_on_error will not suppress/ignore misconfiguration or errors that Home Assistant does not handle.

your error message is an `Unexpected error` those a not handled one.

But yes, the `shell_command` should handle any timeout issue properly, as it is also mentioned in the docs of [shell_command](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/shell_command#execution)

> A 0 exit code means the commands completed successfully without error. In case a command results in a non 0 exit code or is terminated after a timeout of 60 seconds, the result is logged to Home Assistant log.

It would be nice if it was possible to set a timeout for a specific `shell_command`.

Why TimeoutError is Unexpected?..
it is "unexpected" from the code point of view, since it is just not handled. adding a timeout parameter would be a feature request, but proper handling of the timeout should be rated as bugfix.
